Subsequently, obsequies and funeral ceremonies of the deceased was performed by spending more than Rs.4,00,000/.
 4.

It is further stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy,
and was aged about 31 years.
And he was working as Software Engineer at Infosys, Mysore, and used to earn income of Rs.70,000/ per month.

He was  5 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
3 contributing his entire earnings for the maintenance of his family, being the sole bread earner of the family.

Due to the unnatural death of the deceased,
the petitioners' life become dark, miserable and depressed, and put to great financial hardship.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred, due to the negligent act of the rider of the offending vehicle, Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA09HX7006.

In this regard,
criminal case was registered against him, in Crime No.19/2020, for the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C, by the jurisdictional police.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, the petitioners have approached this court, seeking  6 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 compensation of Rs.3,00,00,000/ consequent upon the death of Prashanth.Y.V. in the alleged accident.
 6.

After service of the notice of this petition,
respondent No.1 appeared before the court, but notfiled written statement.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2, has made appearance through counsel and filed written statement, in answer to the ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
4 case of the petitioners.

7. In the written statement of the respondent No.2, not seriously disputed the accident, and the death of the Prashanth.Y.V. But, denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Further, denied the manner of the accident, age, occupation and income of the deceased.

Though the existence of policy pertaining to the offending vehicle was not denied,
stated that, the liability of the respondent is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

And stated that, neither the owner of the vehicle nor  7 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of Section 134(c) and Section158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act in furnishing the better particulars.
It is the specific contention of the respondent No.2 that, the rider of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license, as on the date of the acciden.

As such, he has been prosecuted by the police under Sec.
3(1),181, 5(1), 180 of Motor Vehicles Act and thereby,
there is clear breach of terms and conditions of policy and violation of Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further, contended that, the accident was occurred due to the sole negligence of the deceased, who tried ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
5 to cross the main road without observing the movement of vehicles.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.

With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against the respondent No.2.

sentences.text: I have gone through the propositions laid down in the said authorities, with respect to the liability, when there was no D.L. as on  11 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 the date of the accident and about the principle of pay and recover.

12. On appreciation of the evidence available on record, my findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3 : Partly In the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per the final order,

 *R E A S O N S*
 ISSUE No.1:
 13.

It is the specific case of the petitioners that,
due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
8 registration No.KA09HX7006, alleged accident had taken place.

Consequent upon the said accident,
Prashanth.Y.V., succumbed to the injuries.
The petitioners being the legal heirs of the deceased filed the claim petition against the respondents.

On the  12 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 other hand, though the respondent No.1 & 2 appeared before the court, in response to the notices the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle, was not made an effort to file the written statement in order to disprove the case of the petitioner.

The respondent No.2 being the insurance company, in the written statement though not disputed the accident and the death of Late Prashanth Y.V., seriously disputed the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
14. On going through the above issue, burden is on the petitioners to prove the same, on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities, by placing cogent and convincing evidence on record.

The factum of accident and death of Prashanth consequent upon the accidental injuries and the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased and the involvement of the offending vehicle in the  13 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
9 accident are all not disputed point in issue in the case on hand.
To discharge the burden lies on the petitioner, petitioner No.1 by name Smt.Padma relied on her affidavit evidence, on her behalf and also on behalf of petitioner No.2 & 3.
The PW1 being the mother of the deceased reiterated the main petition averments.
To prove her relationship with the deceased produced documents Ex.P14 to Ex.P18 for consideration.
In proof of the above issue, Ex.P1 to Ex.P8, which are the police records are the material documents for consideration.

15. On taking birds eye view towards the said documents, reflect that, alleged accident had taken place on 25.1.2020, in this regard, PW1 being the mother of the deceased gave first information on the same day.
By virtue of the said information, case has been registered against the rider of the offending vehicle alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.

In  14 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 the recitals of Ex.P1 column No.10 and also in the annexed complaint, there is a clear narration about the the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle to cause the accident.

These documents remained unquestioned by the other side to prove the innocence of the rider of the offending ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
10 vehicle.

If at all, rider of the offending vehicle was innocent, what prevented to him to question the first information well in time, before the competent court of law, in order to prove his innocence nor made an effort to file counter complaint.
These two material documents clearly speak about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.

16. Added to this, on going through the spot mahazar marked at Ex.P3, and spot sketch, Ex.P4 as well as report of the motor vehicle inspector Ex.P5,
inquest mahazar Ex.P6 and P.M. report Ex.P7 go to show that, on the same date of the registration of the case, investigation officer visited the scene of  15 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 occurrence and conducted spot mahazar in the presence of complainant and punch witnesses and prepared spot sketch.

These two documents, give an indication that, due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle accident in question was taken place and seizure of the said motor cycle strengthens the genuineness of the allegation made by the petitioners against the offending vehicle.

As per the report of the inspector, accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in the accident and the damages noted in the said document reflects about the rashness or negligence )

Smt. Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
11 on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle as on the date of the accident.
And Ex.
P6 & Ex
. P7 evident that, due to the accidental injuries, son of the PW1 had died and his corpus was referred for examination

. Though the police papers are not conclusive proof to consider the claim petition, no  16 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 contra materials available on record from the side o the respondents to impeach all these documents.

17. Ultimately, on going through the final report submitted by the investigation officer as per Ex.P8 discloses that, after due investigation process, final report was submitted against the rider of the offending vehicle by name Sandhesh G. by showing him as accused No.1 and also, against the owner of the said vehicle Smt.Monica as accused No.2 on the allegation fully narrated in the column No.17 of the charge sheet to the effect that, the accused No.1 having no valid driving licence was riding his vehicle as on the date of the accident and due to his actionable negligence caused accident and death of Prashanth Y.V. and CW2 by name Srinivas R.
sustained injuries in the said accident.

Accordingly,
he had committed the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 304(A) of IPC and section 3(1) R/W Section 181 of M.V. Act.

Further, alleged ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
12

17 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 in the said charge sheet that, the accused No.2 being the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle, handed over the said vehicle to her son accused No.1, who had no valid driving licence as on the date of the accident.
As such, she has committed the offence punishable under section 5(1) R/W Section 180 of IMV Act.

To impeach this material document, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle or its rider have not appeared before the court to lead rebuttal evidence to shaken the case of the petitioners and their stand against the rider of the offending vehicle.

18. On the other hand, the insurance company had placed the evidence of RW1 B.Basavaraju, police inspector, as per his evidence, final report has been submitted against the rider of the offending vehicle and in this regard, criminal case is pending for consideration.
And as on the date of accident, rider had no valid driving licence.
His evidence remained  18 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 unquestioned.

At the time of crossexamination of the petitioner, this witness answered that, at the time of his investigation process, he collected the materials with respect to the involvement of the ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
13 offending vehicle in the accident, which led him to file charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle.

19. At the time of crossexamination of PW1,
though several questions put to the witness, nothing has been elicited to prove the innocence of the rider of the offending vehicle and to prove the defence of the company that, due to the sole negligence on the part of the deceased, accident in question had taken place.
To prove this defence the respondent company has not made an effort to examine the eye witnesses.

As such, mere suggestion or question in this regard,
holds no water.

Accordingly, I am of the view that,
the petitioners had placed cogent and convincing evidence in support of the above issue.
There are no  19 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 materials to show that the prosecution papers were engineered for the sake of compensation.

20. Over all appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioners, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners herein, with respect to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle, convincing evidence placed on record for consideration.

Though, the respondent company placed evidence to rebut the case of the petitioners,
utterly failed to prove the innocence of the rider of the ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
14 offending vehicle.
As such, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle, Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA09HX7006.
And in the said accident, Prashanth.Y.V, had died.
Added to this, the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased.
Resultantly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

20 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020  ISSUE No.2:
 21.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Since in the death case, the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.
At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P14 to Ex.P18, as stated above, are not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents, clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

22. Another aspect to be considered herein ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
15 that, on going through the age particulars of the petitioners, mentioned in the cause title of the  21 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 petition, reflected that, the petitioner No.1 in her middle age has lost the love and affection of her son and petitioners No.2 & 3 have lost love and affection of their elder brother, who is the main earner of the family.
The respondents herein have not produced documents on record, to show the independent economic status of the petitioners.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents to the deceased during his lifetime.

23. The petitioners herein, to prove the actual age of the deceased, as on the date of the accident,
have placed his Aadhar card at Ex.P17.
On going through same, the year of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 1989.

The said document,
remained unquestioned by the other side.
The alleged accident had occurred on 25.1.2020.
Hence, it is safely to be considered that, as on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged about 31 years.

For  22 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 his age, multiplier '16' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.
 24.

In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition, and also in the ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
16 evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was working as Software Engineer at Infosys, Mysore, and used to earn income of Rs.70,000/ per month.
The same thing has been reiterated in the evidence of PW1.

In support of the evidence of PW1, she produced the death certificate, Aadhar card, PAN card, Marks card,
convocation certificate pertaining to the deceased as per Ex.P11, Ex.P13, Ex.P17 to Ex.P23 respectively.
At the time of crossexamination of PW1, by denying the suggestion of the other side that, her son was earning only Rs.48,000/ to Rs.49,000/ stated that, he used to earn Rs.70,000/ per month.

In addition to this,
the petitioners relied on the evidence of Associate Manager employee of Infosys Corporate office by name Kumaraswamy.
The evidence of this witness  23 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 deposed that, Late Prashanth Y.V. was working in their Organisation at Mysore Unit from 27.1.2015 to 27.1.2020.
And he used to get the salary of Rs.54,946/.
Subsequently, on 27.1.2020 he was relieved from his services due to his death.
And in para No.5 of his affidavit evidence stated that, he also entitled for future increments and promotions.

But at the time of crossexamination in connection with the increments and promotion of the deceased, he admitted that, no supportive documents are ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
17 produced in this regard.
25 . In connection with the salary of the deceased during the accident is concerned, at the time of evidence of PW2 placed 5 documentary evidence marked at examination.
P24 to
Ex .P28

. 
Among them, Ex.P26 is five pay slips.
Accident in question had taken place on 25.1.2020.

As such,
among the 5 pay slips of the deceased, it is apt to taken into consideration of the pay slip of the month  24 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 of December 2019.
At that time, his gross income was Rs.54,946/.
From the said amount if the professional tax of Rs.200/ and income tax of Rs.2,490/ was deducted, it will come to Rs.52,256/.
Hence, the income of the deceased is apt to considered as Rs.52,256/ p.m., which will meet the ends of justice.

26. Another point to be taken in to consideration herein that, as per the petition, since the deceased was a bachelor, for deduction of the personal and living expenses, the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14 is to be considered.

sentences.text: The addition should be 30 per  cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40  and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between  the age of 50 and 60 years
, the addition should  be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as  actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was  selfemployed or on a fixed salary, an addition of  40 per cent of the established income should be  the warrant where the deceased was below the  age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where  the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50  years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the  deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years  and 10 per cent where the deceased was between  the age of 5060 years should be regarded as the  necessary method of computation.
The  established income means the income minus the  tax component.
Having considered the above as per law laid down in the above case.

In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, since the deceased was a bachelor, deduction towards personal and  26 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 living expenses out of the total compensation is to be considered.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 31 years, as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "16" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
19

Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through main petition averments it is evident that, the petitioner herein as on the date of the accident, was not having permanent job.

As such by taking into consideration of the nature of the employment mentioned in the petition, I am of the view that, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.52,256/ per month.
And Rs.6,27,072/ per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased, comes to  27 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 (Rs.6,27,072+2,50,828)= Rs.8,77,900/.

And 50%
has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Thus net loss income comes to Rs.4,38,950/ (Rs.8,77,900 Rs.4,38,950).
This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "16".
Which comes to Rs.70,23,200/ .

sentences.text: In this case, after detailed discussion, with  respect to the proposition laid down in Pappu's  case came to the conclusion that, the insurance  company shall satisfy the claim to the claimants  at first instance and then recover it from the  owner of the offending vehicle in accordance with  law.

38 . In the light of the prepositions laid down in the aforesaid cases, it is relevant to note that, the doctrine of pay and recover has been considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Swaran Singh's Case and in Pappu's case.

And the said judgments of the Honourable Apex Court were not over ruled till today,
 35 SCCH-18 MVC 948/2020 and the propositions laid down in the said judgments, remained intact and the said judgments till today are in force.
Hence, to protect the interest of third party, it is apt in the case on hand, to follow the doctrine of pay and recover.
Since as per Article 12 of the Constitution of India, company also comes under the concept of State.

As such, it is ) Smt.Padma vs ) Monika on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92975180/
26 the duty of the State to protect the interest of the third party.

39. In the light of my detailed discussion held above, I am of the view that, though the respondent No.1, being the owner of the offending vehicle cannot escape from her liability to pay compensation to the petitioner, in view of violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

To protect the interest of the third party, it is necessary to direct the insurance company to pay compensation to the petitioners and thereafter to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle, through due process of law.

As such, the respondent No.2, being the insurance company has to satisfy the award and recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle who is the respondent No.1 in the case on hand, in view of the valid insurance policy.

As such,
the respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Thereafter, recover the same from the owner through due process of law.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 in the Affirmative and the issue No.3 partly in the Affirmative.

 41.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.71,14,100/ (Rupees seventy one lakhs fourteen thousand and one hundred only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 being the insurance company, is liable to pay the compensation determined by this court, with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order, at the first instance, thereafter, recover the same, from the respondent No.1, who is the owner of the offending vehicle, in accordance with law.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitle the share of 70% and petitioner No.2 is entitle the share of 20% and the petitioner No.3 is entitled the share of 10%.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 to 3, shall deposit 40% of their share, in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice, for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to them through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/.
Draw award accordingly.
